GitHub Connection

Connect your GitHub account using a Personal Access Token to manage your repositories.

Scoped to specific repositories, with fine-grained permissions (Contents, Pull requests, Issues, Actions, Secrets, Pages, etc) and a built-in expiry. The safer default for most people. Note: fine-grained tokens can't star repositories.

Scoped by broad permission like repo, workflow and user, across every repository you can access. Needed if you want to star or unstar repositories from GitPilot.

Use a fine-grained personal access token with repo access, plus the permissions for any features you want (Actions, Pull requests, Issues, Secrets, Pages, Security events, Administration, etc). Create a token on GitHub →

Changelog

What's new in GitPilot.

v1.4.0: File Save Fixes Stable

  • Creating a new file now checks the path first, with a clear error if it's taken
  • Fixed a crash where saving could silently overwrite someone else's changes
  • Clearer error messages across every file save, rename and delete action
  • General stability fixes to the Manage repository view

v1.3.0: Dual Token Setup Stable

  • Separate Fine-grained and Classic tabs when connecting, each with guidance
  • Drafts are remembered per tab, so switching never loses either token
  • Polished the connection screen's contrast and borders in dark mode
  • Create Repository panel now matches every other card's full width
  • Manage repository dialog now fully covers the screen on every device

v1.2.0: Repo Manager & Permissions Stable

  • New "Manage" view to browse, open and edit repository files
  • Flip a repo public or private, and control GitHub Pages, from the same view
  • Star or unstar any repository straight from the repo list
  • Clearer permission errors, plus a Settings view of what your token can do

v1.1.0: Polish & Fixes Stable

  • Dropped the install/manifest flow that was crashing on home screens
  • Straightened out Copilot's layout and sizing on mobile
  • Swapped browser-default checkboxes, radios, dropdowns and sliders for a themed look
  • Fixed a rendering bug that shrank checkboxes to nearly invisible

v1.0.0: Stable Release Stable

  • GitPilot graduates from beta to a stable release
  • Introduced Copilot, an AI chat assistant for GitHub help
  • App icon and branding now follow your theme
  • A round of general stability and polish fixes

v0.9.0: One-Time Setup Flow Beta

  • Paste your token once and GitPilot remembers it for next time
  • Token stays in this browser only, never sent elsewhere
  • "Skip for now" lets you dismiss setup without saving anything
  • Token gets validated up front, with a clear error if it fails

v0.8.0: Faster Token Setup Beta

  • Jump straight to GitHub's token creation page from the dashboard
  • Creating a repository now lives in one consistent place
  • Added scope hints so setup goes smoother the first time
  • Better errors when a token is invalid or has expired

v0.7.0: UI Consistency Pass Beta

  • Swept out stray punctuation for a cleaner, plainer tone
  • Version number now matches across every page
  • Dashboard stat cards line up at equal size and height
  • Double-checked that every color follows the active theme

v0.6.0: Fine-Grained Token Support Beta

  • Browse, open, create, close and merge pull requests and issues
  • View and trigger Actions workflows, manage repo variables
  • Create and manage encrypted secrets, turn on GitHub Pages
  • Review and resolve Dependabot and secret-scanning alerts

v0.5.0: Initial Beta Release Beta

  • Connect with a Personal Access Token, validated live
  • Browse, search, sort and filter your repositories
  • Upload files or an entire ZIP straight into a repo
  • A local activity log, with no credentials ever stored

About

GitPilot v1.3.0

GitPilot is an independent, open-source, community-driven companion for working with GitHub repositories. It is not an official GitHub product and is not affiliated with or endorsed by GitHub, Inc. or Microsoft Corporation.

GitPilot talks directly to the official GitHub REST API from your browser. Your token stays with you, and no backend ever sees it.

Project repository Report an issue Contribute

Feedback, bug reports and pull requests are always welcome from the community.

Terms & Disclaimers

  • Token security: sent only to GitHub's API over HTTPS, and Settings shows exactly what your token can do.
  • File editing and visibility: edits, new files, Pages changes and public/private flips made here apply straight to GitHub, with no undo inside GitPilot.
  • Starring: needs a classic token with the user scope, since fine-grained tokens don't support it.
  • Independent project: not affiliated with or endorsed by GitHub or Microsoft, and subject to GitHub's own rate limits and policies.
